ac:layout-cell.p: We want the GENFI app (agent_tools in bravo-agency-app) to follow the DK Jago app (digital_banking_app), the same way as the BFI Mobile assessment. This page compares the two. It lists the gaps and suggests an order of work. GENFI shares one monorepo, one CI setup and 15 shared packages with SQUARE, MyShaf and MY BISPRO, so about half of the findings here are the same on the SQUARE page.

li.p: Three workflows in the repo print secrets, and one more exports the signing keystore. The SIT pipeline has a "Reveal secret" step that prints FIREBASE_API_KEY on every tag push: 162 runs so far, the last on 22 Oct 2026. See the Security items section. This is the first thing to fix.

Architecture is the biggest gap. No domain layer. Controllers call shared_data repositories directly and API models reach the screens. Features import each other freely (129 imports across features (76 not into feature/common); calculator and prospect import each other, and so do convent_registration and account_information).

The monorepo is a good start. Shared data packages per backend service, path dependencies, melos categories per app, and generated code kept out of the hand-written count. But the generated code is 8.7 times the hand-written code and is committed, and six near-identical auth clients live in shared_data.
Analytics: Already close to the target. Missing: a fan-out to Datadog, typed parameters, and MyShaf coverage (Crashlytics and the wrapper are skipped for the Sharia flavour).
Logging is silently broken. DatadogLog.e creates a Datadog logger and never writes to it, so handled errors reach only Crashlytics, and not at all for the MyShaf flavour.
Testing is better than BFI. Controller tests are allowed and exist. But there is no coverage threshold, and no end-to-end tests.
App protection is missing. No RASP, no build registration. Pinning is only on in prod builds.
Decision already made: keep Riverpod. Copy Jago's layers, ports and analytics wrapper, not its bloc library.

p.strong: Where this app sits in the monorepo

ac:layout-cell.p: Effort: S = up to 1 sprint, M = 2–4 sprints, L = more than a quarter. Rows marked (shared) describe the whole monorepo.

td.p: Repo layout
Melos workspace. 4 apps, 49 module_* packages (features + shared), 110 library/* wrappers around pub.dev packages.

Melos workspace: 3 apps + 15 shared packages (shared). GENFI is one package with 34 feature folders under lib/feature. The apps are not members of the root workspace; melos categories list which shared packages each app uses.

Every feature lives in one package. 129 imports across features (76 not into feature/common); calculator and prospect import each other, and so do convent_registration and account_information. Nothing stops it.
L
Layering
data → domain ← presentation in every feature. Domain is pure Dart. Features talk through thin *_api contract packages. Rules are written down in .claude/rules.

Screen → controller (StateNotifier) → shared_data repository → HttpClient. No domain layer. 79 files call a shared_data repository provider directly. 11 screen or controller files take *Response DTOs (e.g. prospect_pbf_detail_screen_controller.dart:68, input_prospect_screen.dart:671). shared_data mostly maps network DTOs to "domain" models, which is a good base.
Business rules sit in controllers and screens. API changes reach the screens directly.
L
State management
bloc, with rules: no BuildContext or navigation inside blocs.
Riverpod 2.6 with the old StateNotifier API: 96 controllers, 104 static final provider. No global appRef (better than BFI). ref.watch inside callbacks: 3.
Keep Riverpod. Move to Notifier / AsyncNotifier.
M
Dependency injection
injectable + get_it. Each module exposes a micro-package. Wiring happens only in the app layer.
Riverpod providers. main.dart overrides HttpClient, NetworkConfig and the auth client per app through ProviderScope.overrides. Shared packages expose providers that throw until overridden.
Riverpod is fine as DI. The gap is ports: shared_data exposes concrete repositories, not interfaces, so nothing can be swapped or faked below the HttpClient.
M (comes with layering)
Analytics wrapper
AnalyticsPlatform interface. One fan-out sends each event to Datadog, Firebase and CleverTap. Events are typed classes.

One wrapper, ConventAnalyticsService: a 5-value enum (login, register, kalkulator, input_prospek, daftar_prospek) and 4 call sites. Firebase only. Datadog RUM gets screen names from a separate navigation observer. Parameter keys are string literals (one typo: "proudct"). User id is bravoAgentId, with marketing_id and marketing_spv_id as user properties.
Already close to the target. Missing: a fan-out to Datadog, typed parameters, and MyShaf coverage (Crashlytics and the wrapper are skipped for the Sharia flavour).
S
Logging and crashes
Monitoring fans out to Crashlytics and Datadog. PII is cleaned by jago_observability_sanitizer.dart.

DatadogLog.e creates a Datadog logger and never writes to it, so handled errors reach only Crashlytics. A comment in main.dart admits this. Crashlytics is off for the Sharia flavour and for web. Crash keys include nik_marketing. Consent is hard-coded to granted. No PII cleaner.
Fix DatadogLog.e (or remove Datadog logs on purpose). Add a PII cleaner. Decide on crash reporting for MyShaf.
S
Feature flags
Typed flag catalogue behind one FeatureFlagPlatform interface. Providers: Firebase Remote Config, Split.io, GrowthBook.

Typed freezed model ConventFeatureFlag (20 keys) plus a nested app-config model (10 keys). Generated code: about 3,900 lines. One raw getBool in main.dart. DEMO_ACCOUNT_PHONE_NUMBERS is delivered through Remote Config. Sharia has a separate 1-flag model. Some flags are still compile-time dart-defines.
One typed catalogue for both flavours, behind one interface. Move compile-time flags into it.
S
Networking
dio adapter behind a client interface. 17 typed exception classes mapped to error messages.

core HttpClient (395 lines, dio) has no auth. Auth lives in OtpHttpClient, a 264-line decorator that checks the token before every call, refreshes with a single-flight guard, and retries once on 401. Five client variants are wired in main.dart (default, auth, Krakend, chat gateway, non-auth Krakend). Alice (debug inspector) is a normal dependency, disabled only at runtime. No outgoing trace id. (shared) Six near-identical auth decorators, 1,508 lines in total, exist across shared_data; only one of them retries after a refresh.
Move auth, refresh and retry into dio interceptors shared by all apps. Keep Alice out of release builds. Send a trace id.
M
Security
Everspin Eversafe anti-tamper, CodeMix code protection on every prod build, each build registered, device fingerprint, screen-capture guard, certificate pinning.

Pinning only when SHA_256_FINGERPRINT is passed, which the SIT and dev pipelines do not do. Root check on by default (git fork of flutter_jailbreak_detection). Play Integrity / App Attest only in the Sharia flavour (FEATURE_INTEGRITY_CHECK). R8 and shrinkResources on, plus --obfuscate, but the referenced proguard-rules.pro is not in the repo. allowBackup and cleartext traffic are off. Debug builds are signed with the release key. http_proxy can be enabled in prod builds by a GitHub variable. No screen-capture guard. No RASP.
Pin in every environment. Run integrity checks for GENFI, not only MyShaf. Add proguard-rules.pro. Remove the proxy switch from prod. RASP needs a vendor.
S (fixes) / M (RASP, needs vendor)
Design system
module_design_library: tokens generated from a Figma export, brand and theme switching, Widgetbook published to GitLab Pages.

Two git design systems from frontend-mobile-ui: ds_2 (154 files) and ds_3 (199 files); 110 files import both. The monorepo ui_theme is not used. BfiColors is used 1,237 times vs 92 raw Colors. A local ds3 shim exists with a "remove after merging to DS3" TODO. (shared) Four design systems are in use across the repo: ds_1, ds_2, ds_3 and ui_theme.
Finish the ds_2 to ds_3 move so one package is enough. No Widgetbook.
M
Testing
About 5,288 test files. Coverage gate on changed files per module. End-to-end tests with Appium + Cucumber on BrowserStack.

149 test files: 665 widget tests and 823 unit tests. 33 controller tests, so controllers are tested directly. No integration or end-to-end tests. No coverage threshold. (shared) Coverage is computed for the whole package and posted as a PR comment with continue-on-error. collab_form has one empty placeholder test; sso, integrity and the pinning fork have none.
Coverage gate on changed files. End-to-end tests for register, prospect and calculator.
M
Lint and guardrails
custom_lint rules, Danger bot, checks for generated files and package use, .claude/rules (14 files) and an mr-review skill.

(shared) Three lint sets: a 1,176-line strict_lint.yaml at the root, very_good_analysis in shared packages, flutter_lints in agent_tools. flutter analyze --fatal-infos in CI. pubghost dead-code check, but dead code and dead translations are allowed. No custom_lint, no architecture rules. Review bots: Copilot code review and a label-triggered Atlas webhook. copilot-instructions.md exists; no .claude/rules.
One lint set. No architecture checks.
S
CI/CD
See the next section.
(shared) GitHub Actions, 31 workflow files on master, 5 disabled. See the next section.
See the next section.
M

ac:layout-cell.p: GENFI's pipelines live in the repo with the other three apps. Tag push *-agent-tools-convent: SIT APK + IPA to Firebase App Distribution (WIF) and a web build to GCS. UAT by manual dispatch. No dev pipeline. The older *-agent-tools workflows are disabled.

td.p: Trigger
Version tag, trigger branches, or manual on master.
Manual dispatch with inputs tag, version and a distribution flag (agent_tools_prod_release.yaml). The branch filter on the dispatch trigger has no effect.
OK.
Toolchain
Flutter version pinned in one place (mise, CI image).
(shared) Flutter 3.35.0 copied by hand into 37 places. No .fvmrc or mise file. Java 11 and 17, Android SDK 33, 35 and 36, and three macOS runner labels are mixed across workflows.
Pin one version in one file (mise.toml or .fvmrc) and read it everywhere. Align Java, SDK and Xcode.
Version and build number
X.Y.Z+W from the tag. Build number from a CI counter.
pubspec.yaml fixed at 1.0.0+1. Typed by the operator and written into pubspec.yaml. No CI counter. Non-prod builds are always +1.
Use a CI counter so the build number always goes up.
Config
dart tools/env.dart writes config per environment. Firebase files are injected.
21 per platform. GEN_AI_WEBSOCKET_URL and DEVICE_INTEGRITY_URL are passed to SIT/UAT or MyShaf but not to GENFI prod. Firebase config files are decoded from secrets.
OK. Review which defines are secrets that end up in the binary.
Build
flutter build appbundle, unsigned. iOS through fastlane.
apk + appbundle with --obfuscate --split-debug-info; iOS through xcodebuild.
Consider fastlane + match for iOS signing.
Code protection
CodeMix on the unsigned bundle, then zipalign, then apksigner.
R8 and shrinkResources on in build.gradle; proguard-rules.pro is missing. No protection step in the pipeline.
Add the rules file. Choose a RASP vendor.
Approval
Prod pipeline lives in a separate repository with its own access.
A job step (trstringer/manual-approval, 2 of 8 named people, using GH_PAT). The _build variant has no approval at all.
Protect the prod environment with required reviewers so every workflow that uses prod secrets needs approval.
Signing
Prod keystore only in the prod pipeline repo.
Keystore and certificates as base64 secrets, decoded at build time.
Acceptable once the artifact upload is gone and the environment is protected.
Distribution
Play internal track (script). TestFlight through fastlane.
Play internal track (only when is_firebase_distribution is false; when true, nothing is distributed for Android). TestFlight always.
Fix the dead path.
Post-build
Eversafe build registration (forgery tracking).
Symbols to Datadog and Crashlytics. The iOS Crashlytics upload path does not match the archive path.
Fix the symbol paths. Add registration once a RASP vendor is chosen.
PR checks
Lint (+ custom rules), format, generated files, package rules, tests with random order, coverage on changed files, Danger.

(shared) Format, analyze, pubghost, tests, coverage comment. Runs only when *.dart files change: a PR that touches only .github/**, pubspec.yaml, Gradle or iOS files runs no checks. No coverage threshold. No test randomisation. No generated-files check. Conventional commit titles are asked for in the PR template but not enforced.
Run checks on every PR. Add a coverage gate on changed files and a generated-code check.
Release
Tag from the release branch.
(shared) tag-release-pipeline runs standard-version as bfibravo-bot with a PAT; the app is picked by matching text in the tag name. Only master exists; no release branches.
OK, but the tag-to-app matching is fragile (any tag containing "are" goes to are_tracker).

core contains Flutter UI (reference_id_block.dart builds an AlertDialog). HttpClient maps the stream and plain response types to json.
Generated code in shared_data: 658 files, 291,420 lines, against 33,497 hand-written lines (8.7x), all committed. The largest single generated file is 8,238 lines.
Seven TODOs in prospect_list_controller.dart say "Convent part still using dummy data". Check whether any dummy data reaches production.
android/app has both build.gradle and an unused template build.gradle.kts (debug signing, "id.co.agent_tools"). Delete the template.
ref.watch is called inside onPressed callbacks in 3 places, and inside the router builder. These cause rebuilds on every change.
The web build (convent-web pipeline) deploys to a GCS bucket marked TODO in the workflow. Decide whether the web target is supported.
README still lists a bfi_design_system folder and mockito; neither matches the repo.
Translations: Indonesian only (app_id.arb). No sync tool. Low priority unless an English version is planned.
AI rules: .github/copilot-instructions.md exists. Add .claude/rules for the layer rules and an mr-review skill, shared across the three BFI mobile repos.
graphify-out/ (48,755-node generated code graph) is committed and refreshed weekly by a workflow with contents: write. Decide whether it belongs in the repo.

ac:layout-cell.h3: 1. Workflows that print or export secrets (urgent)
ac:layout-cell.p: Three workflows in this repo echo secrets through sed 's/./& /g', which puts a space between every character. GitHub hides a secret in logs only when the exact value appears, so the spaced-out value is readable by anyone who can open the run log. The same pattern was found in bravo-customer-app on 9 Oct 2026.

ac:layout-cell.p: What this means for GENFI. The convent SIT pipeline (agent-tools-convent-deploy-tag-cd-pipeline.yml, lines 94-95) prints FIREBASE_API_KEY with the same sed trick on every tag push. It has run 162 times; the latest run was 22 Oct 2026.

li.p: Delete test.yaml and debugger.yaml from master. Delete the "Reveal secret" step from the convent SIT pipeline and the keystore upload step from the SQUARE pipeline.
Rotate FIREBASE_API_KEY for the SIT Firebase project. It has been printed in 162 run logs.

Rotate SSH_PRIVATE_KEY, BRAVO_GCP_SA_KEY and KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET in every environment that debugger.yaml names, and the prod keystore password. They were exposed to anyone who could run the workflow, and that is the safe default.

Add required reviewers to the four prod environments (agency_prod_agent_tools, agency_prod_are_tracker, sharia_prod_myshaf, sharia_prod_mybispro) and to prod_ro_tools, so no workflow can use prod secrets without approval. (Not verified: the current rules could not be read from this session.)
Add a CI check that fails any workflow which echoes secrets.* or uploads a keystore, and run it on PRs that change .github/**.
Check the other mobile repo, bravo-ro-tools-apps, for the same files.

Prod builds without environment protection (not verified). The approval is a workflow step, not an environment rule, and agent_tools_prod_release_build.yaml builds a prod-signed APK and IPA with no approval. The environment settings could not be read from this session.
Pinning is off in SIT and dev builds, because those pipelines do not pass SHA_256_FINGERPRINT. Testers run unpinned builds, and a pinning bug would only show in UAT.
The proxy switch (FEATURE_ENABLE_PROXY) is passed into prod builds from a GitHub variable. If it is ever true, prod traffic can be routed through a proxy.
Play Integrity / App Attest only runs for the Sharia flavour. GENFI, the larger app, has no device integrity check.
proguard-rules.pro is referenced by build.gradle but not in the repo. Check what the release build really applies.
The certificate-pinning fork passes every request header, including Authorization, to native code and prints channel arguments. The fork is excluded from analysis and has no tests.
Crash reports carry nik_marketing as a custom key. Treat it as personal data.
Tracking consent for Datadog is hard-coded to granted in main.dart (all three apps). Tie it to a real consent setting.
Secrets are interpolated straight into run: commands in several workflows, and inputs are used unquoted in shell. Pass them through env: instead.

Every third-party action is pinned by tag, and fjogeleit/yaml-update-action by the main branch (22 uses). The reusable update-graphify workflow runs from bfi-base-template@master with secrets: inherit. Pin by SHA.
Most workflows run with the default token permissions; only the WIF jobs set permissions: explicitly.

ac:layout-cell.p: Start with prospect and calculator (the two largest features, 6 files over 1,800 lines).

Pure-Dart entities and use cases. shared_data repositories sit behind ports. Screens never see API models.
Shared dio interceptors
Auth, refresh, retry and trace id move out of the six decorators into core. One refresh guard.

td.p: RASP / code protection
Vendor chosen (Everspin, or another). A protection step in the prod pipeline. Each build registered. One decision for all three BFI mobile repos.
One design system
GENFI finishes ds_3; SQUARE moves from ds_1; ui_theme retired or merged. Widgetbook published.
End-to-end suite
Main journeys covered on real devices: register, prospect input, calculator, reserve lead.
Shared-package cleanup
One Keycloak repository, one token store, dead packages removed, generated code out of git or split.

li.p: Who owns this plan? The squad that owns agent_tools (Agency), with a named tech lead. The shared plans (security, CI/CD, networking, lint, repo layout, design system) need one owner across the four apps in the repo.
RASP vendor and budget. The decision should cover bravo-customer-app, bravo-agency-app and bravo-ro-tools-apps together.
Coverage threshold. What number for changed files? A suggested start is 70%, raised over time.
Generated code. 291,420 generated lines in shared_data are committed. Generate in CI instead, or split the largest models?
Is the web build of GENFI a supported target? It changes what the pinning fork and Alice can do.
Does MyShaf stay a flavour of agent_tools, or become its own app? It already has its own pipelines, environments and integrity check.
